pr_body:
# Objective

- Fixes #11933.
- Related: #12280.

## Solution

- Specify that, after applying `AmbientLight`, the resulting units are in cd/m^2.
- This is based on [@fintelia's comment](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/11933#issuecomment-1995427587), and will need to be verified.

---

## Changelog

- Specified units for `AmbientLight`'s `brightness` field.
pr_comments: Since I don't believe there is a clear conclusion to this, I'm going to close the PR. If a consensus is reached (or I'm misunderstanding), please let me know. :)

I think this is good to merge as is. It isn't a complete explainer of the relevant color theory ([my comment](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/13297#discussion_r1596151189) goes into a bit more detail), but ultimately that discussion probably doesn't belong in the doc comment anyway.

issue_context.title: AmbientLight docs doesn't specify units
issue_context.body:
## How can Bevy's documentation be improved?

The documentation for `AmbientLight`s brightness field says:

> A direct scale factor multiplied with `color` before being passed to the shader.

However, it would be helpful to know the units of the product of multiplying color and the scale factor. I suspect the unit is either lux or nits, but I haven't investigated
comments:
`brightness` is a multiplier, so it itself does not have any units. It was originally added in #1605, where it calculates:

```rust
(ambient_light_resource.color * ambient_light_resource.brightness)
```

Which is equivalent to a `Vec4 * f32`. On main, it currently looks like:

https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/a9ca8491aa3f2dc99116e63d67a0625afe6e738d/crates/bevy_pbr/src/render/light.rs#L983-L984

You could say the same thing about the skybox's [`brightness`](https://docs.rs/bevy/0.13.0/bevy/core_pipeline/struct.Skybox.html#structfield.brightness) field. The documentation I'm looking for is the analog of this line:

> Scale factor applied to the skybox image. After applying this multiplier to the image samples, the resulting values should be in units of [cd/m^2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candela_per_square_metre).
That's a very good point. So would `AmbientLight::brightness` also be in cd/m^2, or would it be some other unit?
Looking at the code I think @fintelia ’s last comment is the correct answer.

Marking this as a good first issue. [`AmbientLight`](https://dev-docs.bevyengine.org/bevy/pbr/struct.AmbientLight.html)'s brightness field should document that it is in [cd/m^2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candela_per_square_metre), similar to [`Skybox::brightness`](https://dev-docs.bevyengine.org/bevy/core_pipeline/struct.Skybox.html#structfield.brightness), if I'm understanding @superdump's comment correctly.

Maybe it would also be good to specify that this is *not* equivalent to Filament's [IBL](https://google.github.io/filament/Filament.md.html#lighting/imagebasedlights/iblunit), even though the units are the same and they are both used for global illumination.

@janhohenheim my understanding is that if one sets bevy’s ambient light brightness to 1 then it would be the same. Or you can consider the combination of color * brightness to be the same as Filament’s IBL.

@superdump I'm very skeptical because per https://github.com/google/filament/issues/1667, Blender's background shader is the same as IBL, but my testing in https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/12280 reveals that it does not correspond at all to an `AmbientLight` when using a strength of 1.
Of course, I might be wrong in how I export stuff from Blender, so take this with a grain of salt.

review_comments: Is it that straightforward? Does it depend on the color type? Is alpha ignored? How can I get the total brightness from each channel?
I don't know; I was just following the comments in the issue. @fintelia or @superdump, could you comment on this?

First the color gets converted to linear sRGB  (if necessary) and scaled by the brightness:
https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/4da11fda77f58b9ebe126c92747a6666e530d7d5/crates/bevy_pbr/src/render/light.rs#L985-L986

Then the alpha channel gets completely ignored via a swizzle and the RGB channels are used for rendering calculations:
https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/4da11fda77f58b9ebe126c92747a6666e530d7d5/crates/bevy_pbr/src/render/pbr_ambient.wgsl#L28

Interpreting the meaning of the three values in the RGB channels is a much deeper rabbit hole. My non-expert understanding is that a value like (100.0, 100.0, 100.0) corresponds to a total light intensity of 100 cd/m^2 divided up as 21 cd/m^2 of red light, 72 cd/m^2 of green light, and 7 cd/m^2 of blue light. Where the colors precise meanings of "red light", "green light", and "blue light" are given by the sRGB spec and the relative weights also come from that same spec

Based on its usage in [prepare_lights](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/4da11fda77f58b9ebe126c92747a6666e530d7d5/crates/bevy_pbr/src/render/light.rs#L985), the ambient light is always converted to `LinearRgba` (so colour space does not matter), and the colour passed to the GPU is this colour scaled by brightness.

So, we could either say `Color` is unitless (a scalar) and `brightness` is in `cd/m^2`, or the reverse. I _think_ we want to say `Color` is unitless because it conceptually makes more sense that `brightness` is the intensity value (candela/square-metre).
